name: Chunyu Yi pulse diagnosis in the Shiji
description: The Shiji memoir of Chunyu Yi describes a diagnostic approach involving examination of the pulse and records medical case histories.

impact.note: One text witnessing pulse examination and case records in early Chinese medicine, a practice continued by later physicians in that tradition.

date.label: Shiji conventionally dated about 86 BCE
date.basis: The date is scoped to this described observation, text, archaeological interpretation or object, not the origin of the wider practice.

events.statement: The Shiji memoir of Chunyu Yi describes a diagnostic approach involving examination of the pulse and records medical case histories.

evidence.supports: Hsu interprets the Chunyu Yi memoir in chapter 105 of the Shiji as an early extensive account of pulse-based diagnostic reasoning and dates composition conventionally around 86 BCE while warning of complex textual history. Only the publisher’s introductory excerpt was inspected, not the complete translation or a contemporary manuscript.

Hsu’s preface dates the Shiji to about 86 BCE and identifies the memoir in chapter 105 as an extensive account of pulse diagnosis with 25 medical case histories. This is a conventional date for the history, not the date of a surviving manuscript or proof that transmitted wording is original. Only the front matter and preface were inspected.

events.caveats: The date is a conventional estimated composition date of a transmitted text, not a surviving manuscript date or precise date of each patient encounter. Hsu describes a complex textual history; only the introductory excerpt was read, and no modern diagnostic validity is assumed.
